claims.text: Applying metadynamics during thermal processing of an RHEA-Cu composite enables a self-sustaining, large-scale reaction.
Metadynamics produces a stable, homogeneous RHEA-Cu microstructure by overcoming thermodynamic demixing.
A positive heat of mixing between refractory elements and Cu predisposes the precursor composite to phase segregation.
Metadynamics can explore the free-energy landscape of the material during high-temperature processing.
Free-energy-landscape sampling triggers reaction pathways that bypass demixing barriers.
Sufficient thermal energy allows the RHEA-Cu system to sample alternative reaction pathways while mitigating phase segregation.
Overcoming free-energy barriers causes transient metastable phases and nucleation sites to develop.
Transient metastable phases and nucleation sites mediate formation of a homogeneous composite microstructure.
Metadynamics physically drives the reaction system through free-energy barriers.
Metadynamics identifies and stabilizes processing windows in which refractory elements and Cu react cohesively rather than segregate.
Targeted free-energy sampling reduces the kinetic penalties associated with positive heat of mixing.
Targeted free-energy sampling reduces the thermodynamic penalties associated with positive heat of mixing.
The proposed processing method yields a large-scale, uniform RHEA-Cu microstructure with reduced phase segregation.
Reduced phase segregation enhances the composite's high-temperature structural stability.
Reduced phase segregation enhances the composite's irradiation stability.
Conventional processing of RHEA-Cu composites causes significant phase segregation and unstable microstructures because of positive heat of mixing.
The method requires sufficiently rapid diffusion and adequate free-energy sampling to be effective.
Slow intrinsic diffusion or processing-scale limitations can prevent exploitation of the optimized reaction pathway.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis asserts that the method enables a large-scale reaction and large-scale uniform microstructure, while the uncertainty field states that successful scaling from laboratory to industrial production is unknown.
